story.title: Chelsea Secures 4-3 Victory Over Brighton in Premier League Match
story.summary: Chelsea triumphed over Brighton with a score of 4-3 in a thrilling Premier League match, continuing their strong performance under new manager Xabi Alonso. This victory marks Chelsea's third consecutive win, including two in the league and one in the League Cup since Alonso took charge.

explore_lenses.label: How did Chelsea turn a rout into a close win?
explore_lenses.title: Fast attack, then a difficult defensive spell
explore_lenses.summary: Chelsea built a 3-0 lead in 32 minutes, but Brighton repeatedly found space after the break; Palmer's 74th-minute goal restored breathing room before Brighton's final stoppage-time strike.

claims.text: Lavia, Neto and Joao Pedro gave Chelsea a three-goal lead by the 32nd minute; Yalcouye scored before halftime, Joao Pedro then scored an own goal, and Palmer made it 4-2 before Gross's 90+6 goal.
Chelsea made three substitutions during Brighton's second-half pressure and later shifted to a 5-4-1 shape to protect the lead.
Chelsea's report said the open second half was likely more open than Alonso wanted, while the Guardian's match analysis argued Brighton exposed system shortcomings.

story_report.summary: Chelsea began Xabi Alonso’s tenure with a 4-3 Premier League win over Brighton, extending a perfect three-match start across league and League Cup competition. The result gave Chelsea six points from their opening two league games, although the narrow finish followed a match in which Brighton mounted sustained second-half pressure. Chelsea’s immediate next test is an away match against Arsenal at the Emirates on Sunday, September 6.

sections.heading: Chelsea’s Brighton Match Swung Late
sections.body: Chelsea built a three-goal lead within 32 minutes through Lavia, Neto and Joao Pedro. Yalcouye scored before halftime, while a Joao Pedro own goal reduced the margin before Palmer restored Chelsea’s two-goal advantage at 4-2. Brighton continued to press, prompting three Chelsea substitutions and a later switch to a 5-4-1 shape; Gross scored in the sixth minute of stoppage time to complete the 4-3 scoreline.

sections.heading: Arsenal Away Tests Alonso’s Start
sections.body: Chelsea will travel to Arsenal for a Premier League match scheduled for 16:30 BST on September 6, with the club identifying the Emirates fixture as its next game after Brighton. Al Jazeera described Arsenal as Alonso’s first major test following wins over Fulham, Luton and Brighton. The match offers an early indication of Chelsea’s level, but cannot by itself settle questions about the team’s season-long standing.

unresolved.text: It remains unclear whether Chelsea’s defensive vulnerability against Brighton reflected a tactical issue, player integration or the short-term effects of protecting a lead.
Chelsea’s title prospects cannot be reliably inferred from two league matches; the assessment will remain incomplete before the Arsenal away fixture.

related_stories.title: Iceland Votes to Reject EU Membership Talks in Referendum
related_stories.summary: In a recent referendum, Icelanders voted against reopening talks for European Union membership, with 52.8% of voters rejecting the proposal. The decision halts the government's efforts to revive accession discussions, emphasizing concerns over the protection of Iceland's fishing waters. The outcome reflects a divided public opinion on the issue.
